card.name: Verb after a patient group or disease
card.fires_on: The linking verb (are, is) or the article 'a' right after a subject such as 'elderly patients', a disease name, or a patient group in a warning sentence. It marks the spot just before a statement about risk or disease nature.

modes.label: After patient group
modes.description: 'are' follows a group of patients or a drug-treated group, before a risk statement.
modes.example: Because elderly patients<< are>> more likely to have decreased renal function,

modes.label: After disease name
modes.description: 'is' or 'a' follows a disease name as a definition begins.
modes.example: Panic disorder<< is>> a chronic condition, and it is reasonable

modes.label: After drug interrupter
modes.description: 'are' follows a patient group with a drug list set off by commas.
modes.example: Patients receiving immunosuppressants, including Mycophenolate Mofetil,<< are>> at increased risk of developing bacterial, fungal

card.writes: It seems to steer the next word toward descriptive terms like chronic, heterogeneous or intentional.
